text:
marcos: APAC GPU warm pool struggling to join in ap-southeast-1 after yesterday's egress lock. ~15% fail with KMS/HSM errors and warmup spinning. Noticed cost spike from retries.

leah: Any bootstrap logs?

marcos: Snippet from kubelet bootstrap: 
```
2026-03-24T02:05:12Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/gpu-node-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:222222222222:key/xyz-1234
Caused by: PrincipalNotFound or credential handshake to hsm-proxy timed out
```

ops-sre: Hmm HSM-proxy? We recently moved keystore traffic via privatelink to hsm-proxy.internal. Was the privatelink endpoint in this account?

leah: The privatelink endpoint was created in a shared-services account, but the DNS record for hsm-proxy.internal resolves to the shared ENI. However, our endpoint policy denies cross-account run unless explicit principal in the KMS key policy exists. So nodes try privatelink -> HSM returns auth error -> fallback to NAT blocked by FW.

sec-compliance: We tightened NAT earlier to cut S3/KMS direct. We approved privatelink-only but didn't catch cross-account key policy gap.

ops-sre: Options: (1) add the gpu-node-role principal to the KMS key policy in shared-services (needs change freeze exception), (2) create a short-lived delegated grant from control-plane prior to node decrypt, (3) temporarily allow NAT egress for keystore IPs for a short TTL.

marcos: Cost/ops: warm pool is churning, hourly wasted GPU time ~120 GPU-minutes/hr while nodes retry. If we open NAT even briefly we'll incur egress and extra S3 write costs for audit logs.

leah: Could we instead have the control-plane create a one-off grant and attach it to the provisioning token in SSM so node can use it during first decrypt? That avoids key policy edits and NAT.

ops-sre: We can implement grant creation: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:222222222222:key/xyz-1234 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/gpu-node-role --operations Decrypt --name provisioning-grant-temp --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={"purpose":"node-provisioning"}
```
Control plane would retire the grant after 10m.

sec-compliance: Prefers grant approach or key policy change. NAT allowlist only with logging and max 30m. If you choose grant, add audit event for grant creation+retire and require signed change approval for any key policy edits.

marcos: I'm +1 for grant path. Who can wire control-plane to call create-grant in sequence with node bootstrap?

leah: I can add a create-grant step to the provisioning controller. Quick patch: pre-create grant when we generate the bootstrap token and store grantId in SSM parameter encrypted. Node uses bootstrap token -> control-plane signals grant available -> decrypt. I'll mock in staging first. ETA ~70m.

ops-sre: Meanwhile we'll mitigate risk: enable a tiny NAT allowlist scoped to the provisioning subnet + KMS FQDNs for 20 minutes, enable VPC flow-logs to locked S3 and CloudTrail for grant events. If things look stable, we'll close NAT and rely on grant.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-1046 - "apac gpu warm-pool fail: hsm/privatelink auth errors". PD: @ops-sre.

marcos: Tagging canary: provisioning:canary=true and add metric provisioning.time_to_decrypt. If decrypt > 30s mark failed.

leah: Adding unit/integration tests for grant lifecycle and a healthcheck that verifies privileged decrypt path before marking pool healthy. Will also add a dashboard for wasted GPU-minutes during onboarding.

sec-compliance: Approving short NAT for 20m with flow-logs. Keep me posted and paste grant audit events once retired.

ops-sre: Rule IDs when created: FW-1901 (allow egress to kms.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com from subnet-xyz for 20m). Monitoring: if join failures drop below 3% and retry CPU < 5% extend not needed.

marcos: Working on metric snapshot now. Current join failures: 18/120 nodes (15%) last 15m, warm-pool churn +1.2 GPU-hrs lost. Will post status update in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
